reviews.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Approving `5545f5a3`. It fixes the CRLF part of #1743, and main (`1e575ab0`) still has the bug. We built main and this head and ran both on a team clone with `core.autocrlf=true`, delivery records deleted, then a team update plus a `skills/.removed` entry:

| Case | main | this head |
|---|---|---|
| Unedited CRLF copy after a team update | kept as not teamai's | updated |
| Skill listed in `skills/.removed` | left in place | removed |
| Member's CRLF copy with a content edit | kept | kept |
| Member's CRLF copy with only a trailing-space edit | kept | kept |
| `doctor` | lists teamai's own copies as kept | lists only the member's edited copies |

A copy the member converted from CRLF to LF and nothing else is overwritten on both, so nothing changes there.

[P2 non-blocking] A copy that matches no version now costs two git processes per historical version: `git cat-file --filters` in `readRenderedBlob`, then `blobIdOf` on the result. Those are mostly the member's edited copies, which every `pull` and `doctor` re-checks. One file with 300 versions went from 53 ms to 4.9 s on macOS, and process start is slower on Windows. A cheaper shape is one `git hash-object --path=<path> --stdin` of the candidate. It applies the same clean filter in reverse, so its id can be compared with `versions` by blob id like the fast path. Batching `--filters` reads is harder: `git cat-file --batch --filters` prints the unfiltered size in its header, so the size-based parser in `readBlobs` does not carry over.

[P3 nit] With git-lfs tracking skill files, `--filters` runs the LFS smudge for every old version that falls through, which may fetch old objects. We did not run this.

The CI review (https://github.com/Tencent/teamai-cli/pull/1764#issuecomment-6683270054) reports no findings. We agree that there is no correctness defect. It does not cover the cost above.
